items.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: he had played with Rudy Vallee’s orchestra back in the 1920s so he knew a lot of those old songs and like that.

ctx.x: You mentioned Wild Bill Davison and I wonder, do you fit yourself into a line of trumpet players do you think? Were there people that you listened to when you were coming up learning the instrument, that became part of your sound?

Oh yeah. I mean every musician who plays improvised music goes through this, I mean you have to in order to — improvising, creating an improvising style is kind of like creating your personal language. And you have to kind of put together your vocabulary. It’s kind of a language that only you speak. And you put it together out of various things that you hear around you. And so sure, I mean I played nothing but classical music until I was almost finished with college. But I always listened to a lot of jazz,…
Was there one particular person, a jazz trumpeter that made you really sit up and say that’s somebody I’d really like to sound like? © Fiillius Jazz Archive -3-
